Keep a level-order control in step with its column

Source: R/level_order.R
setup_level_order.Rd

The server half of level_order_input(). Refills the control with the levels of the selected column whenever the data or the column changes, holds the order the plot should use, and restores defaults[[inputId]] when the module's Reset button (input$reset) is pressed.

Usage

setup_level_order(
  input,
  session,
  data,
  column,
  defaults = NULL,
  inputId = "x.order",
  max.levels = 20
)

Arguments

input, session

The module's input and session.

data

A reactive holding the module's data frame.

column

A reactive (or function) giving the name of the column ordered, e.g. reactive(input$x.data).

defaults

The module's named list of defaults, or NULL.

inputId

The un-namespaced ID of the level_order_input().

max.levels

The most levels the control offers; see level_order_choices().

Value

A shiny::reactiveVal() holding the levels in the order to draw, or NULL for the default order. Hand it to apply_level_order().

Details

A new column starts from defaults[[inputId]] (levels it does not have are ignored), and new data for the same column keeps the order the user dragged the levels into. A column the control cannot order – numeric, or with more than max.levels levels – empties the control, which hides it.

The returned store, not input[[inputId]], is what the plot should read. It changes only when the order to draw does, so neither the control reporting its initial value nor its echo of an update costs an extra render. A defaults[[inputId]] given as a shiny::reactive() is followed as the parent's state changes, as with setup_reactive_defaults().

See also

level_order_input(), apply_level_order()

Author

Jared Andrews

Examples

if (interactive()) {
    library(shiny)

    ui <- fluidPage(
        selectInput("x", "X", c("Species", "Petal.Size")),
        level_order_input("x.order", "X Order"),
        plotOutput("plot")
    )

    server <- function(input, output, session) {
        data <- reactive({
            df <- example_iris
            df$Petal.Size <- ifelse(df$Petal.Length > 4, "Large", "Small")
            df
        })
        x.order <- setup_level_order(input, session, data, reactive(input$x))

        output$plot <- renderPlot({
            df <- apply_level_order(data(), input$x, x.order())
            boxplot(df$Sepal.Length ~ df[[input$x]], xlab = input$x)
        })
    }

    shinyApp(ui, server)
}
